title.narrative: Pathways to Inclusive Development: Bridging Data, Participation, and Human Rights for the Localization of SDGs

description.narrative:
The project endeavours to strengthen participatory data collection and monitoring processes through digital data platforms and foster coordination for advancing SDG localization within a human rights-based framework. It addresses the gap of “Monitoring: limited data, lack of monitoring and reporting capacities, and little evidence-based analysis” as defined by the Local2030 Coalition and focuses on the SDG transition of “digital transformation.”
The project is structured around three interconnected areas: 1. Capacity development on SDG localization: The project strengthens capacities of public officials to effectively localize SDGs through monitoring and reporting, participatory planning, and financing to achieve the transformative potential of the 2030 Agenda, emphasizing human rights principles, and inclusive, accountable processes with OHCHR. 2. Digital systems for localized SDG monitoring and reporting: UN-Habitat will review data systems and support an urban observatory in Irbid, integrating SDG indicators through a human rights and gender-based approach. UN-Habitat and UNDP will accordingly adjust the Ministry of Interior’s Tanmiah platform, the Department of Statistics’ Jordan Development Portal, and other data systems to mainstream SDGs, improve data reporting and policy coherence, and enhance coordination between statistical offices. 3. Advocacy at the heart of participatory development: UN-Habitat, with OHCHR, will enhance the awareness of communities through digital channels, including podcasts and social media to communicate about the six transitions in non-technical language. This will empower communities to participate in decision-making, advocate, and take initiative for SDG localization.
This collaboration positions Jordan to effectively localize and advance the 2030 Agenda, whereby advocacy informs actions, driving data-driven monitoring.
